notes: 20 events per role, disjoint topic set from prototypes.json. Authored after prototypes.json was frozen.

events.text: Approved Stripe over Square as the primary payment processor after the merchant-fee analysis.
Switched search infra from Elasticsearch to Vespa to support hybrid queries.
Adopted Kotlin Multiplatform for the shared mobile-data layer.
Settled on Triton for ML serving over a custom FastAPI implementation.
Replaced RabbitMQ with NATS for the high-throughput event bus.
Chose Cloudflare over Fastly for the global CDN tier.
Committed to S3 plus R2 dual-write for new uploads.
Switched authentication from session cookies to JWT for the public API.
Approved the move to per-seat billing for enterprise plans.
Selected SES over SendGrid for transactional email.
Adopted a two-tower retrieval model over collaborative filtering.
Decided to integrate Sift Score for chargeback prevention.
Approved migrating analytics off Snowplow to Segment.
Settled on Argo Rollouts over Flux for canary deployments.
Switched APM from New Relic to Datadog after the renewal cycle.
Adopted Karpenter as the cluster autoscaler over Cluster Autoscaler.
Chose React Server Components over a Next.js custom setup for the marketing site.
Approved GraphQL over gRPC for the public-facing API surface.
Replaced the self-hosted Postgres with Aurora for the production cluster.
Adopted Temporal over Cadence for workflow orchestration.
Investigating why the Stripe webhook latency spiked 4x last Tuesday.
Looking into why search relevance dropped 6% after the index rebuild.
Diagnosing the increased crash rate on Android 14 devices.
Examining why ML model latency varies 10x across availability zones.
Root-causing the Kafka consumer lag that started this morning.
Trying to understand why the CDN hit rate dropped from 94% to 81%.
Investigating the spike in S3 GetObject latency p99.
Diagnosing why JWT verification fails intermittently in the auth microservice.
Looking into the discrepancy between billing reports and actual usage.
Examining the email delivery rate dip in the EU region.
Investigating why the new recommender shows zero results for power users.
Root-causing the false-positive spike in our fraud-detection model.
Looking into why analytics events are arriving 30 minutes late.
Trying to understand why rolling deployments occasionally hang.
Investigating the gap between application metrics and infra metrics.
Diagnosing why nodes drift from their desired pool size during peak.
Examining the Lighthouse score drop on the home page.
Looking into the recent uptick in 504 timeouts on the public API.
Investigating slow query patterns that emerged after the schema migration.
Root-causing why scheduled jobs occasionally fire twice.

Search QPS climbed 40% week-over-week after the homepage redesign.
Mobile session duration measured up 12% on iOS post-update.
ML inference latency p95 holds steady at 45ms across all regions.
Queue depth metrics show off-peak idle increased to 30 seconds average.
CDN bandwidth usage shows a clear lunchtime spike pattern in EMEA.
Object count in the primary bucket crossed 10 billion this month.
Failed login rate stable around 2.1% over the past 30 days.

Email open rates ticked up to 27% after the template refresh.
Recommendation CTR data shows a flat line across personas this week.
Fraud chargeback rate dropped to 0.04% after the rule update.
Analytics events ingested per day plateaued at 2.3B.
Deployment frequency report shows 14 deploys per week median.
Alert noise metrics show 22% of alerts auto-resolved within 5 minutes.
Cluster autoscaler logs indicate scaling events doubled this week.
Frontend bundle size measured at 312 KB, up 8% from baseline.
API request mix shows mobile clients are now 62% of traffic.
Database CPU utilization peaks at 78% during the nightly batch.
Scheduled job runtime distribution shows a long tail above 5 minutes.
Personally I would prefer keeping Stripe and just absorbing the fee bump.
Recommend Elasticsearch over Solr for this use case despite the cost.
Lean toward shipping native apps rather than a Flutter rewrite.
Would rather invest in better serving infra than a new model.
Team's preference is Kafka for everything; it's already in the stack.
Advocate for sticking with one CDN even though multi-CDN is theoretically better.
My take is to keep S3 as source of truth and treat R2 as a cache.
Prefer keeping session cookies for the web app despite JWT advantages.
Recommend per-user billing for SMB and per-seat for enterprise.
In favor of consolidating to SES; SendGrid's reliability has been mixed.
Lean toward a hybrid recommender over pure embedding-based.
Would rather block more aggressively and refund false positives than miss fraud.
Personally I would argue for self-hosted analytics over vendor lock-in.
Prefer canary deploys with manual gates for production-critical services.
My preference is to ship Grafana over the vendor dashboard for SRE workflows.
Recommend investing in observability before adding more infra capacity.
Lean toward TypeScript-first; the velocity hit is worth the safety.
